column1: # Tier-1 platform case ledger for the compiled-build CI gates.
# This table names the compiled-build behaviour the task acceptance criteria
# require each runner to execute.  `.github/ci/platform-case-gate.sh` enforces
# it against a real `go test -json` stream:
#   * every row listing this GOOS in `must_run_on` must be observed PASSING.
#     A rename, a deletion, a `-run` filter matching nothing, a missing
#     interpreter or an unset conformance root all fail here by name instead
#   * a skip of a listed case -- or of any of its subtests -- is FATAL unless
#     a row tolerates it on this GOOS.
#     each target GOOS, that every case a row requires is actually compiled
#     into that platform's build, and that no platform where a case IS
#   package  test  must_run_on  skip_allowed_on  class  behaviour
# `test` may name a subtest (`Parent/child`) or use the `Parent/*` form, which
# tolerates a skip of any subtest of `Parent` while still requiring `Parent`
# itself to pass.  `must_run_on` / `skip_allowed_on` take a comma separated
# subset of {linux,darwin,windows}, or `-` for the empty set.
# `class` records WHY a tolerated skip is legitimate and is checked against
# the reason text the test actually printed:
#   platform-control  a control rc5-native-control-inventory-v1 defines for
#                     another platform only -- the AC's explicit carve-out
#   host-capability   the runner filesystem cannot create the artefact the
#                     vector needs (symlink, hard link, reparse point, FIFO,
#   root-content      the supplied conformance root publishes no such vector
#   opt-in            an explicit developer environment variable
# A GOOS on which the case's package is excluded by the supplied conformance
# root's own qualification vector (see `.github/ci/suite-plan.sh`) is neither
# required nor an omission: the exclusion is asserted positively by the
# rejection case at the bottom of this file.
